title: Amenorrhea
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with oligomenorrhea/amenorrhea, hirsutism, acne, obesity, and infertility. PCOS is the most common endocrine disorder in reproductive-age women. Rotterdam criteria (need 2 of 3): (1) oligo/anovulation, (2) clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism (hirsutism, acne, elevated free testosterone), (3) polycystic ovaries on ultrasound (≥12 follicles 2-9mm per ovary or ovarian volume >10mL). Other causes of hyperandrogenism must be ruled out: late-onset CAH (check 17-OH progesterone), androgen-secreting tumor (rapid virilization, very high testosterone), Cushing's, hyperprolactinemia. Labs: LH:FSH ratio >2:1 is classic but not diagnostic. Associated with insulin resistance → screen for diabetes (glucose, HbA1c, OGTT). Treatment: weight loss (first-line, improves all parameters), combined OCPs (regulate cycles, reduce hyperandrogenism), metformin (insulin sensitizer, improves ovulation), spironolactone (anti-androgen for hirsutism). Clomiphene or letrozole for ovulation induction if fertility desired.
chief_complaint: Irregular periods, hirsutism, acne, difficulty conceiving
